terminus.sourceSays: The dissertation argues that public-land management exceeds registry cleanup and includes use, revenue, disposition and intergovernmental allocation. At the same time, it says deeper analysis followed by classification can identify the core of management problems and support bounded problem-setting and solutions. It also notes that traditional single-domain policy classification is insufficient for complex cross-domain public-land management.
terminus.method: non-care-domain counterexample + internally opposed reconstruction of the prior LEGIBILITY CASCADE candidate
terminus.generated: MUTHER revision: LEGIBILITY IS BIDIRECTIONAL. Better recognition does not inherently enlarge intervention scope. It can produce at least two opposed moves: CASCADE, when newly visible dependencies recursively recruit additional domains; and COMPRESSION, when classification/partition makes a large field decisionable by isolating a tractable core. The key variable is therefore not diagnostic depth alone but what the recognition operation does to relations: dependency-discovery expands the action graph, while decision-partition can contract it. This is a MUTHER synthesis, not Liu Wei-jeen's stated model.
terminus.novelty: important counterexample that prevents legibility cascade from becoming a one-way law; converts it into a bifurcating mechanism
